### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7ed8e3b38f0a9e85ca355d145fd132402e0e977` — the merge of head `58698caa351d546295248ade5a30c1040e140262` into base `a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f7ed8e3b38f0a9e85ca355d145fd132402e0e977 && git checkout f7ed8e3b38f0a9e85ca355d145fd132402e0e977
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216 58698caa351d546295248ade5a30c1040e140262 && git checkout -B drift-repro a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216 && git merge --no-ff 58698caa351d546295248ade5a30c1040e140262

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f4a273bb49a3e5cdf79ffb1884c318a60da1c8bd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.permission-write-without-read-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/access-upgrade-report.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/access-upgrade-check.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.writeImpliesRead.test.tsx, .changeset/sec-hardening-u-write-implies-read.md, content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx

Delta review by the same reviewer, on top of the FAIL record at `d7bf39c3301c73fb62829b966a9c9f7350cae1d4`. Inputs: `git diff d7bf39c3..f4a273bb` (one commit, 4 files, 77 / 9), the rewritten PR body read in full, and the check-runs on `f4a273bb` — all ten required contexts `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI). Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run. Every judgment of the earlier record that the delta does not touch stands as written there.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The must-fix is cleared.** The body's "Out of this rule, unchanged" bullet now carries only "`allowCreate` and `allowTransfer` without read". Re-read in full against §6: title, body, changeset, D3 entry, docs pages, the new commit message ("unticking View All or Modify All clears Edit and Delete once nothing reads; the upgrade report's edit cell reads through the fold") and every test name stay at rule level. No disclosure remains.
- **`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`.** The read-off cascade now fires on unticking any bit that reads (`unticksARead`: Read, View All or Modify All, value `false`) and clears Edit and Delete only when no reading bit is left on the entry (`!allowRead && !viewAllRecords && !modifyAllRecords`). That is exactly the schema's predicate, in both directions: cleared iff the entry would otherwise carry `allowEdit`/`allowDelete` with no read, kept while any reading bit remains (so the #25575 pair is never authored beside Modify All). Four new pins cover the stored entries the first record named (`{ viewAllRecords, allowEdit, allowDelete }` and `{ allowEdit, allowDelete, modifyAllRecords }` → both cleared, payload parses) and the reverse (View All off keeps Edit/Delete while Read, or Modify All, still reads). The first record's should-fix is closed.
- **`access-upgrade-report.ts`.** Both edit reads go through `grantsEditBit` = raw `allowEdit` ∧ `objectPermissionGrants(entry, 'allowEdit')`, i.e. the declared bit ∧ read. Keeping the raw bit as a conjunct is right for this report: its question is whether a customer set's own edit grant meets a package field deny, and widening the cell to `modifyAllRecords` alone would report super-user entries whose field semantics are a different question (the dev's FLS reason). A stored set granting edit without read is no longer reported as lacking an edit deny (pinned in `access-upgrade-check.test.ts`, beside a reading control that still is). The last enforcement-adjacent raw read is gone; the should-fix is closed.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the first record: `@objectstack/spec` minor with `!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, ADR-0087 marker and FROM → TO, D3 entry, no D2; `@objectstack/plugin-security` minor and `@object-ui/app-shell` minor cover the two files the delta touches. No generated artifact is affected by the delta (no schema, no public export); the regenerated reference pages from the earlier head stand.

**The dev's open question — should the changeset's `ui/` bullet name all three reading bits? Yes.** The changeset ships as the `CHANGELOG.md` sentence an upgrading author greps, and at this head it (and the `ui/` bullet of the PR body, and the `In Setup` sentence of `permission-sets.mdx`) still describe the narrower cascade of the previous head: "unticks Edit and Delete when Read is unticked (unless View All or Modify All still grants the read)". That sentence is still true, so it is not a contract breach, but it under-states what shipped. State the rule as the code and its test header now do: ticking Edit or Delete ticks Read; unticking any bit that reads — Read, View All or Modify All — unticks Edit and Delete once no bit that reads is left. Should-fix, see ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- §6: clear on this head (see ①).
- **Should-fix (prose, three places):** (a) the changeset's `@object-ui/app-shell` bullet, the body's `ui/` bullet and the docs' `In Setup` sentence — name all three reading bits as above; (b) the body's acceptance note "`access-upgrade-report.ts` still reads the raw `allowEdit` bit … Noted, not changed" is now false at this head and contradicts the delta — replace with the `grantsEditBit` statement; (c) the Verification section names `403f77c0` / `d7bf39c3` only and reports `PermissionMatrixEditor.writeImpliesRead` as 5 / 5 where the head carries 9 — name `f4a273bb` and its readings, or say the head's check-runs are the measurement. None of these changes a contract; (a) edits the changeset and so takes one more head and a fresh record at it, which the seat may fold together with (b) and (c) or accept as noted.
- Residuals (2) and (3) of the first record: unchanged by the delta, still follow-ups through §3 with the two maintainer questions named there (ruling C; ADR-0066 ⑤).
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list.

### ④ Design judgment

- The two spec `hits` are untouched by the delta; the first record's judgment on them stands.
- `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` against `ObjectPermissionSchema`'s refusal: holds — the editor can no longer hand either save door an entry the schema refuses through any single tick or untick, and every pin reads the saved payload and parses it.
- `access-upgrade-report.ts` against the fold and the report's own question: holds — declared bit ∧ read, deliberately not the super-user widening, with a pin for the stored unread shape.
- No must-fix. Should-fixes: the three prose alignments in ③.

**VERDICT: PASS**

  - Transfer without read: goes to the maintainer as a separate decision. Not changed here.

- **Gates (dev):**
  - `--ran`: 113 run and 0 NOT MEASURED at `f4a273bb`; 54 run and 0 NOT MEASURED at `58698caa`.
  - Full suites: spec 812 files, plugin-security 242, runtime 543.
  - Dogfood battery: 417/421 files, 1 load timeout that passes when run alone.
